findings.title: TypeScript `token_errors` includes `MemoryError`, which contradicts the slice's failure-mode table
findings.description:
- **The conflict:** Task 14 makes the TypeScript tokenizer's `token_errors` `TypeScriptParseError` and `MemoryError`. This copies the length pipeline's error tuple (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/typescript_length.py:151`). But Task 10 and the slice's failure-mode table (row 2) say a `MemoryError` during the duplication pass makes `duplicated_lines` `tool_failed`. Task 11 tests exactly that.
- **What happens as written:** in the TypeScript adapter, a `MemoryError` would be caught as a per-file error. The file goes into `unparsed_files` and the pass carries on, producing the kind of partial figure D3 forbids.
- **The languages also disagree:** Python's tokenizer leaves `MemoryError` out of its token errors (Task 12), even though `_PARSE_ERRORS` at `python_adapter.py:81` includes it.
- **Fix:** remove `MemoryError` from Task 14's `token_errors`. Add a Task 15 test showing that a `MemoryError` from the TypeScript tokenizer gives `tool_failed`.

findings.title: `read_coverage`'s result type is described inconsistently across Tasks 19, 21 and 23
findings.description:
- Task 19 returns "a failure (not an exception)", and Task 21 also produces failures (stat `OSError`).
- But Task 21 then says "The result is either a reading or an absence (reason, detail)".
- Task 23 handles three cases: an absence, a failure (sent to `tool_failed`) and a reading.
- A junior implementer could fold failures into absences with a made-up reason, or drop the failure case.
- **Fix:** state the result as reading | absence | failure in Task 21, and name the failure type once in Task 19.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes, not plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description:
- Every commit line (Tasks 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30) is written as `- [ ] Commit: ...`.
- Commit markers must be plain `**Commit**: ...` lines. As checkboxes they get checked off like work items, and they invite a commit that only checks a box.
- Where they sit is fine: each one comes at a tested, working point.

findings.title: The token-ceiling test doesn't check that the language's other metrics are unchanged
findings.description:
- Success Criterion 10 and the Technical Requirement ("assert both the signal and the outcome for each row") include "its other metrics are unchanged".
- Task 11 tests the ceiling only at the `duplication.py` level.
- One adapter-level assertion would close this: lower the ceiling with `monkeypatch`, then check that function length and complexity are still present. It fits in Task 13 or Task 26.

findings.title: Duplication's `unparsed_files` won't appear in the summary
findings.description:
- Task 27 renders `duplicated_lines` with the generic "N in M file(s)" branch, and that branch never shows `unparsed_files`.
- The API Contracts example doesn't show it either, so this isn't a gap against the slice. A tokenizer failure will only be visible in the JSON and the WARNING log.
